_comment: Four parts, at least two players each. No transposition: each part's phrase entry lists the pitches that part may choose from, and those are the keys that light up on the piano. Write them as names (Eb3, G#4, A2) or as MIDI numbers, and fractional numbers for anything off the 12-tone grid — 57.5 is a quarter-tone above Bb2. An empty or missing notes list frees the pitch entirely. tractDelta is added to the phrase preset's tract length: the lower parts get a bigger body as well as lower notes. All instruction text is placeholder.

phrases.instruction: PLACEHOLDER — enter first, on either pitch. A, held, letting each vowel find its own length. Do not hurry the /s/.
PLACEHOLDER — silent until the lower parts have cracked twice, then answer once with T.
PLACEHOLDER — E on single words, sparse. Change pitch between words, never during one.
PLACEHOLDER — sustain. Hold the last vowel of each word until you run out of breath.
PLACEHOLDER — Q only. Scattered phonemes, no words. Either pitch, changing freely.
PLACEHOLDER — quarter-tones: sit between the other parts and stay there.
PLACEHOLDER — repeat with A. Move between the two pitches without warning.
PLACEHOLDER — last to stop. Let the final /l/ fade alone.
PLACEHOLDER — join Part 1 after their second word, S rate.
PLACEHOLDER — R, once, sharply, then silence for the length of a breath.
PLACEHOLDER — W on random words. Let them land between Part 1's.
PLACEHOLDER — S throughout, drifting behind Part 1.
PLACEHOLDER — alternate Q and T, irregular.
PLACEHOLDER — quarter-tones, beating against Part 1. Do not correct the beating.
PLACEHOLDER — A, very slow, one phoneme per breath.
PLACEHOLDER — fade out first, mid-phrase, mid-word.
PLACEHOLDER — D rate, speaking, under the upper parts.
PLACEHOLDER — the CRACK is yours. R twice, hard, then let the others answer.
PLACEHOLDER — the text in full, S rate; the only part that is intelligible here.
PLACEHOLDER — T only. Percussion under the sustained parts.
PLACEHOLDER — W on the next word each time, in order, slow.
PLACEHOLDER — quarter-tones. Let the vowels bend as far as they will.
PLACEHOLDER — trade words with Part 4, one each.
PLACEHOLDER — hold the final consonant closure. Release only when Part 1 does.
PLACEHOLDER — lowest, almost subsonic. One word for the whole phrase.
PLACEHOLDER — silent. Choose any pitch and wait.
PLACEHOLDER — T, sparse, felt more than heard.
PLACEHOLDER — sustain a single vowel. Move only when Part 3 moves.
PLACEHOLDER — Q, slow, one every few seconds.
PLACEHOLDER — quarter-tones, whispered (whisper on).
PLACEHOLDER — trade words with Part 3, one each.
PLACEHOLDER — in unison with everyone, then stop halfway through.
